previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, type 2 diabetes, cardiomyopathy due to Chagas disease, and a history of coronary artery bypass grafting was admitted for acute gallstone pancreatitis. He presented with right upper quadrant pain, nausea, and vomiting, and was found to have elevated lipase and gallstones on ultrasound. He was managed conservatively with IV fluids and pain control while optimizing his blood pressure with increased lisinopril and addition of isosorbide mononitrate for surgical clearance. He underwent a laparoscopic cholecystectomy, during which he experienced transient bradycardia and a temporary junctional rhythm that resolved without intervention. Postoperatively, he had mild nausea but tolerated a regular diet and recovered well. His medications were adjusted, including continuation of Imdur and increased simvastatin, while reverting to his prior lisinopril dose. He received hemodialysis as scheduled and was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up plans.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo male with ESRD on HD (MWF), CAD s/p CABG, CHF last EF 30% 
secondary to Chagas, who presents with bradycardia and 
hypotension found to have significant hyperkalemia.

# Hyperkalemia: Pt presented with potassium of 8.6 from his HD 
session. Unclear etiology of the hyperkalemia though one 
possibility was he left his HD session prior to completion. He 
reports being compliant with his diet with out any deviation. He 
has been on lisinopril, although he has been on it since ___. 
Potassium returned to normal level after dialysis. His cardiac 
meds were restarted but his lisinopril was reduced to 40mg 
daily.

# Bradycardia/Hypotension: Unclear etiology and improved after 
treatment for hyperkalemia in the ED with calcium. He did 
require atropine and dopamine gtt in the ED. ECG showed 
idioventricular rhythm with slow response. Possible etiologies 
include electrolyte abnormalities. No evidence of infection on 
CXR and no fever or leukocytosis and therefore unlikely sepsis. 
He did report some mild diarrhea. The patient has mildly 
elevated trop in the setting of renal failure. No chest pain. 
Continued on aspirin. Home blood pressure meds initially held 
and then restarted once blood pressures stabilized. Blood 
cultures drawn and were pending at the time of discharge.

# ESRD: On ___ HD. Last dialysis was on ___. See above for 
hyperkalemia. Renal consulted. Continued on calcium acetate and 
cinacalcet as well as nephrocaps. Discharged with plans for HD 
on day after discharge.

# DM: Briefly hypoglycemic after 10U insulin in the ED but 
normalized after 1 amp of D50. Continued on Q6H ___ and an 
insulin sliding scale. His lantus was held at first and then 
restarted prior to discharge.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ man with shortness of breath and hypotension,
evaluate for pneumonia.

COMPARISON:  Portable AP chest radiograph ___.

PORTABLE AP CHEST RADIOGRAPH:  There is moderate cardiomegaly.  The patient is
status post CABG with sternotomy wires midline and intact.  There is minimal
pulmonary vascular engorgement.  Right pleural effusion is unchanged from ___.  A new small left-sided pleural effusion is noted.  Increased
opacification at the right lung base may represent layering pleural effusion,
or atelectasis; however, infectious process cannot be completely excluded in
the correct clinical setting.  Bilateral lung volumes are low.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Right-sided pleural effusion, unchanged. Small left-sided pleural effusion
is new since prior.
2.  Density at the right lung base may be secondary to layering pleural
effusion; however, atelectasis or infectious consolidation cannot be
completely excluded and should be considered in the correct clinical setting.
3.  Moderate cardiomegaly with mild pulmonary vascular engorgement may
indicate mild congestive cardiac failure.

HISTORY:  End-stage renal disease and pleural effusions.

FINDINGS:  In comparison with study of ___, there is better definition of
the right hemidiaphragm, consistent with some improvement in the atelectasis
in this region.  Enlargement of the cardiac silhouette persists.  The degree
of elevated pulmonary venous pressure appears to have decreased.  The right
pleural effusion with loculation along the lateral chest wall is essentially
unchanged.  Dense streaks of atelectasis in the left mid zone are also
unchanged.
